Agavi, hoe all ye men that round the citadel and shining towers of ancient Tebedwell.
Come, look upon this prize, this lion's spoil, that we have taken ye, with our own toil,
we Cadmus' daughters.
Not with leathern set the salient javelins, not with hunter's net, only white arms and
swift hands bladed fall.
Why make ye much adieu and boast with all your armourer's engines?
See, these palms were bare that caught the angry beast and held and tear the limbs of
him.
Father, go bring to me my father.
I, and Pentheus, where is he, my son?
He shall set up a ladder-stare against this house, and in the triglyphs there nail me
this lion's head, that gloriously I bring ye, having slain him I, even I.
